requirements.requirement: Restore the invoices named in restore-request.txt into live/ with archive-identical bytes and file modes.
requirements.summary: The request names INV-100.txt and INV-101.txt. Both were selectively extracted into live/invoices/, directly compared byte-for-byte with their archive entries, and shown with mode 0644 matching the archive. The same results persisted after restart.

requirements.requirement: Retain the current contents of the newer live/customer register.
requirements.summary: live/customers.csv retained its original 52-byte content and SHA-256 digest before extraction, after extraction, and after restart; the digest also matches the preparation baseline.

requirements.requirement: Do not restore unrelated archived files.
requirements.summary: Although the archive also contains customers.csv and old-notes.txt, the complete post-restore and post-restart live file inventories contain only the pre-existing customer register and the two requested invoices.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 before and after the work. The restore used the existing tar utility successfully, with no package or platform mutation evident.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence. The requested invoices have the correct bytes and modes, the newer customer register is unchanged, no unrelated archive files were restored, and the OS/kernel were preserved. The mandatory node restart was also fully evidenced and the restored state recovered correctly.
limitations: Requirement preserve_customer_register cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The archive extraction was the required task mutation (cmd-083b69c6963148e8). Temporary verification files were bounded and removed by traps (cmd-5fd85ebfa6a04ad8, cmd-6a1aaabc7e4848f2). The scheduled restart served the mandatory provider evidence protocol (cmd-507ce850ad35495b); its transient units did not leave reported residue. Read-only polling and diagnostics caused no evidenced mutation. Afterward there were no failed services, package inconsistency, new network exposure, or unexplained temporary residue. The restart protocol is complete: pre-restart identity and healthy observations, restart acknowledgement, a changed post-restart identity corroborated by the fixed snapshots, running system state, and persisted task data were all captured.
